name: Morphological Profile Analysis
description: Computes multi-scale morphological profiles (opening/closing) for structural anomaly detection in AI-generated images.
mechanism:
This method applies mathematical morphology at multiple scales to characterize image structures and detect anomalies indicative of AI generation or manipulation:

1. **Morphological Opening Profile**: The grayscale image is processed with a series of morphological openings using disk-shaped structuring elements of increasing radius r ∈ {1, 2, 3, ..., R_max}. Opening γ_r(I) = δ_r(ε_r(I)) (dilation of erosion) removes bright structures smaller than 2r. The opening profile OP(r) at each pixel records how pixel intensity changes with increasing r. The derivative dOP/dr indicates the scale at which each structure is removed, providing a multi-scale structural decomposition.

2. **Morphological Closing Profile**: Similarly, closing φ_r(I) = ε_r(δ_r(I)) removes dark structures smaller than 2r. The closing profile CP(r) complements the opening profile by characterizing dark structures (holes, shadows). Together, OP and CP form the Morphological Profile (MP), providing a complete scale-dependent structural representation.

3. **Differential Morphological Profile (DMP)**: The derivatives DOP(r) = OP(r) − OP(r−1) and DCP(r) = CP(r) − CP(r−1) capture structures at each specific scale. In natural photographs, the DMP exhibits characteristic statistics: heavy-tailed distributions at fine scales (many small structures) and sparse distributions at coarse scales. AI-generated images often show more uniform DMP distributions, reflecting the neural network's tendency to produce regular structures across scales.

4. **Structural Anomaly Detection**: For each pixel, the 'characteristic scale' s* = argmax_r |DMP(r)| identifies the dominant structural size. The spatial distribution of characteristic scales is analyzed: in natural images, s* varies smoothly with content (fine s* in textured regions, coarse s* in smooth regions). In manipulated or AI-generated images, transitions between structural scales are abrupt or inconsistent with scene content. A chi-squared test compares local s* histograms against the global distribution to identify anomalous regions.
parameters:
Structuring element: disk-shaped
Radius range: r = 1 to 20 pixels
Radius step: 1 pixel
MP dimensions: 2 × R_max per pixel
Anomaly detection block: 32×32 pixels
Chi-squared significance: α = 0.01
Minimum image size: 128×128 pixels
accuracy: 77–85% accuracy for AI-generated image detection using MP features. DMP-based texture classification achieves AUC of 0.86 for GAN-generated images. Structural anomaly detection localizes manipulated regions with F1-score of 0.80. Performance is strongest on images with varied structural content and weakest on uniformly textured scenes.
source: Pesaresi, M. & Benediktsson, J. A. (2001). A New Approach for the Morphological Segmentation of High-Resolution Satellite Imagery. IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, 39(2), 309–320.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated images through multi-scale structural analysis. Identifying manipulated regions with inconsistent structural characteristics. Texture-based classification for distinguishing natural from synthetic content. Scale-dependent structural characterization for image forensics.
strengths:
• Morphological operations provide intuitive, geometrically meaningful features
• Multi-scale analysis captures structures at all relevant sizes
• Rotation invariant with disk structuring elements
• Computationally efficient with fast morphological algorithms
• Provides interpretable structural decomposition of image content
limitations:
• Disk structuring element does not capture elongated structures (use line SE variants)
• Performance depends on structuring element size range — too small misses large structures
• AI-generated images with realistic multi-scale structure evade detection
• Heavy JPEG compression alters fine-scale morphological profiles
• Uniform regions produce flat MP profiles with no discriminative information
